newsitem.title: CHINA: China, Glencore dispute on the mend - traders.
newsitem.headline: China, Glencore dispute on the mend - traders.

text.p: Ties between China's metals authorities and Glencore were damaged by a rift over zinc quality but are on the mend after bridge-mending meetings and a statement by the Swiss company, traders said on Wednesday.

Glencore and China's state metals trading and producing corporations have been locked in a dispute that industry sources said threatened the Swiss trader's relationship with China and could have led to a total break in ties.

But three days of meetings between Chinese and Glencore officials had gone a long way to mending damage done, traders said, and had been followed up with a statement by Glencore on Wednesday that it had no pending claim against Chinese zinc.
The dispute centred around a quality check Glencore had made on China's London Metal Exchange (LME) registered Torch brand zinc at the request of a customer.
An official of the China National Nonferrous Metals Industry Corp (CNNC) said a complaint had been made against 100 tonnes of Torch zinc ingots which harmed China's interests and reputation.
Trade sources said CNNC sought an apology and may have sent a notice to its subsidiaries suggesting they suspend business with Glencore, which has extensive interests in China, trade sources said.
Glencore's statement, released in London, said the company had acted upon a customer request to perform an analysis on the Chinese zinc and it was found to conform to contractual specifications.
"In the spirit of mutual cooperation and benefit between Glencore and the CNNC group, Glencore intends to develop their long-term relationship with CNNC," the statement said.
"Obviously it has hurt (Glencore's) China position because there are a lot of contracts to be executed," an industry source in Beijing said.
But CNNC subisidiaries were not the company's only Chinese customers, he said on condition of anonymity.
"(Glencore has) a lot of non-CNNC customers, China is so big and there are a lot of customers here," he said.
He said relations between CNNC and Glencore had been improved by the meetings in Beijing, with a recognition on both sides that no long-term business relationship could be without problems.
"Everyone approached the problem constructively," he said, adding that China accounted for a "very important, significant volume" of Glencore's worldwide business.
An official of the Zhuzhou smelter, which produces Torch zinc, told Reuters the quality claim was unjustified.

Another Chinese official said on Wednesday that if there was any move to suspend business with Glencore it could also be part of a general move away from reliance by Chinese producers on traders and towards establishing direct links with customers.
Using intermediaries to market Chinese metal was expensive, she said, and links had already been established with Southeast Asian buyers as the market became more transparent.
